source_refs.note: Topic 11.2.3 (Nomenclature of cycloalkanes) with Figure 11.3, printed page 249.

blocks.text: Cycloalkanes are named by attaching the prefix cyclo- to the name of the alkane with the same number of carbon atoms. Figure 11.3 shows ethylcyclohexane; isopropylcyclohexane (IUPAC 1-methylethylcyclohexane); n-propylcyclohexane (IUPAC propylcyclohexane); and 1,1,4-trimethylcyclohexane, where the ring is numbered to give the substituents the lowest locants.

blocks.caption: Named cycloalkanes (Figure 11.3)
rows: number twice for two groups on C1, lowest locants

blocks.prompt: Give two differences between the molecules of cyclopentane and pentane, and draw the formula of methylcyclohexane (Quick Check 11.1b, c).
blocks.explanation: Cyclopentane C5H10 has its five carbons in a ring with two fewer hydrogens than pentane C5H12, whose carbons form an open chain; the ring has no CH3 end groups while pentane has two. Methylcyclohexane is a six-carbon ring (C6H11) with one CH3 attached: C7H14.

items: Cycloalkane = cyclo- + alkane name with the same carbon count: ethylcyclohexane, (1-methylethyl)cyclohexane, propylcyclohexane, 1,1,4-trimethylcyclohexane.
